hook_text: You owe five suppliers R15 000. Pay them in the wrong column and your stock doubles on paper.
clip_script: October. Ridgeview Hardware owes five suppliers R15 000. Time to pay. Money out of the bank, so the cash payments journal. Each payment, twice: Bank, and Creditors control. Not trading stock. That stock was already counted when it was bought. Office Hub 600. BuildMart 5 800. Toolquip 2 000, part payment. Highveld 4 200. Glow Signs 900. That is 13 500 to creditors. Plus wages 2 800 and stock bought for cash 3 300. Total out: 19 600. Each supplier's page goes down on the debit side. Meanwhile 9 600 of new credit purchases. Control: 15 000 plus 9 600 minus 13 500. 11 100. Supplier pages: 6 500, 1 500, 3 100. 11 100. Match. Debt down. Trust up.
visual_style: Five supplier folders with balances shrinking as EFTs fly out, a red warning when stock nearly gets counted twice, two R11 100 totals snapping together.
pacing: Quick payments montage, one warning beat, one matching finish.
call_to_action: Watch the full lesson and record Ridgeview's October payments yourself.
